subject: Television & Streaming
title: Nat King Cole and the Color Barrier
description: A 60-second lesson on Nat King Cole and the Color Barrier.

hook.text: In 1956, Nat King Cole became the first Black performer to host a national TV variety show. It lasted only one year.

buildup.text: Cole was one of the most popular musicians in America. His talent was undeniable. But sponsors wouldn't touch the show.

discovery.text: Advertisers feared losing Southern white audiences. No national sponsor would back a show with a Black host.

twist.text: NBC canceled the show due to lack of sponsors. Cole said: 'Madison Avenue is afraid of the dark.'

climax.text: Cole's show proved that television's barriers weren't about talent—they were about money, fear, and institutional.

punchline.text: America's best singer wasn't good enough for America's sponsors.

quiz.question: Why was Nat King Cole's TV show canceled despite his popularity?
options: National sponsors refused to back a show hosted by a Black performer
